biography.plain_text: Jorge Emilio González Martínez is a Mexican politician nicknamed El Niño Verde. He succeeded his father as president of the Ecologist Green Party, led it for a decade and served repeatedly in Congress as both deputy and senator. His enduring influence lies in shaping the party's alliances and national legislative presence.

long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Mexico City into a politically connected family, González Martínez studied business administration and environmental management before entering public life through the Partido Verde Ecologista de México. His father, Jorge González Torres, had founded the organisation; the younger González began as an electoral secretary and won a seat in the capital's representative assembly.

His career crossed the Chamber of Deputies and Senate, at times coordinating the Green caucus. In 2001 he took the party presidency, a transfer that made family succession central to his public identity. Over the following decade, the PVEM joined changing national coalitions and established itself as a durable congressional force. González left the formal leadership and later took further federal mandates, including another Senate term and a return to the lower house. Subsequent reporting continues to portray him as an influential power broker, even when he holds no official party or legislative post.
